project.name: 01_POC
project.description: Proof-of-concept study of a 60 kW solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) plant that uses 39 days of plant logger data to split operation into stages, analyse every sensor per stage, generate synthetic plant data, and run a 2D browser-based digital twin.

nodes.name: heater_temps.py
nodes.summary: Joins the five gas-line heater signals (ERH, EAGH, EAOH1-3: control/safety temperatures and currents) onto the decided plant stages and draws one stack-vs-heater figure per stretch of consecutive days; backs heater_temperatures.ipynb.

nodes.name: load_heaters
nodes.summary: Loads one day's heater control/safety temperatures and currents as 1-min means, dropping -1 fill values.

nodes.name: plant_days
nodes.summary: Labels every day file with the plant stages (keeping the old operating_states stage) and returns per-day minute tables and stage blocks.

nodes.name: heater_states
nodes.summary: Joins a day's plant-stage minutes with its heater signals.

nodes.name: stage_table
nodes.summary: Builds a stage-by-heater summary table from a column-name format string.

nodes.name: stretches
nodes.summary: Splits day files into stretches of consecutive calendar days.

nodes.name: heater_panels
nodes.summary: Plots stack temperature against fuel-side and off-gas heater thermocouples on given axes.

nodes.name: plot_stretch
nodes.summary: Draws one figure per day stretch: stack vs heater temperatures shaded by stage plus a stage band, and saves it.

nodes.name: plant_stages.py
nodes.summary: Defines the eight decided SOFC plant stages (Heat-up air through Trip: purge) on top of operating_states.py and industrial_stages.py trip windows, labels every logged minute, and writes the 1-min stage parquet plus a stage-blocks table.
nodes.languageNotes: Rule-based stage labelling done with vectorised pandas masks rather than a row loop; module also acts as a CLI via __main__.

nodes.name: base_stage
nodes.summary: Assigns each minute a plant stage from air, forming gas, natural gas and string current, ignoring trips.

nodes.name: trip_kind
nodes.summary: Classifies a trip cut as emergency stop or purge per the component sensor map.

nodes.name: add_trips
nodes.summary: Overwrites trip windows with Trip: purge or Shutdown (emergency stop until air returns).

nodes.name: label
nodes.summary: Adds the plant_stage column to a minute table by combining base stages and trip windows.

nodes.name: blocks
nodes.summary: Splits a minute table into contiguous runs of one stage, ending a block on logger gaps over 6 h.

nodes.name: episodes
nodes.summary: Merges stage blocks into episodes without No data gaps and records the stage before and after.

nodes.name: transitions
nodes.summary: Counts how often each stage is followed by each other stage.

nodes.name: rule_210_check
nodes.summary: Checks the share of minutes where forming gas on matches stack above 210 C with no natural gas.

nodes.name: per_day
nodes.summary: Tabulates minutes or block starts per day file and stage.

nodes.name: plot_band
nodes.summary: Draws a coloured stage band from a blocks table on a date axis.

nodes.name: legend_handles
nodes.summary: Returns coloured legend patches for the given stages.

nodes.name: run_all
nodes.summary: Segments every day file with operating_states and labels it with plant stages and trip windows.

nodes.name: save
nodes.summary: Labels all days and writes the 1-min plant stage parquet and the stage blocks CSV.

nodes.name: slopes_jerk.py
nodes.summary: Re-runnable slope, bend and jerk analysis of stack, heater and every logged column per plant stage and at every stage border across 39 day files; feeds the twin's bend panel and easing tools.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of pandas resample/rolling/groupby and numpy polyfit for least-squares slopes; parts are selectable from the command line.

nodes.name: _days
nodes.summary: Lists the raw day files to process.

nodes.name: load_frame
nodes.summary: Builds or loads the cached 1-min frame of plant stages, stack, flows, current, power and heater/gas-path temperatures for all days.

nodes.name: load_all_columns
nodes.summary: Builds or loads 1-min means of every raw logger column across all day files.

nodes.name: slope_group
nodes.summary: Maps each minute to its plant stage, splitting Air-flow cooling into normal and strong air.

nodes.name: block_ids
nodes.summary: Assigns block ids that change on label change or logger gaps over 2 min.

nodes.name: stage_runs
nodes.summary: Returns integer positions of every stage block, optionally dropping unclean stretches.

nodes.name: line_slope
nodes.summary: Least-squares slope in units per hour, NaN when fewer than five points.

nodes.name: window_slope
nodes.summary: Slope of a time series between two timestamps.

nodes.name: centred_rate
nodes.summary: Centred-difference rate in C/h over a window, NaN where the window is not continuous.

nodes.name: band
nodes.summary: Bins temperatures into 100 C bands.

nodes.name: stack_block_slopes
nodes.summary: One row per stage block with stack line-fit slope, net slope, start/end temperature and air level.

nodes.name: summarise_blocks
nodes.summary: Median and range of stack block slopes per stage group.

nodes.name: stack_rate_table
nodes.summary: Median stack rate per stage group and 100 C band.

nodes.name: onset_lags
nodes.summary: Minutes from a stage start until the stack has moved 2 C in the expected direction.

nodes.name: _cut_at_gap
nodes.summary: Truncates a run at the first logger gap.

nodes.name: heatup_runs
nodes.summary: Follows each Heat-up air start to measure hours to gas switch and to 100/200/300/500 C.

nodes.name: cooling_runs
nodes.summary: Follows each Air-flow cooling start above 400 C and measures first-hour and three-hour drops.

nodes.name: other_curve_slopes
nodes.summary: Per-block slope, first-30-min change and onset for every heater and gas-path temperature.

nodes.name: column_kind
nodes.summary: Classifies a logged column by its tag prefix into measurement kind.

nodes.name: column_area
nodes.summary: Returns plant area and unit for a logged column.

nodes.name: sensor_descriptions
nodes.summary: Reads tag, property and group per column from the Excel sensor list if present.

nodes.name: all_column_slopes
nodes.summary: Slope of every live logged column in every clean stage block, then the median per stage group in units and percent of range per hour.

nodes.name: _smooth
nodes.summary: Centred rolling mean smoothing helper.

nodes.name: border_shape
nodes.summary: Computes slope before/after, step, peak speed, acceleration and jerk around one stage border.

nodes.name: bend_time
nodes.summary: Minutes for the smoothed stack slope to move 10 to 90 percent from old to new slope at a border.

nodes.name: _grid
nodes.summary: Reindexes the frame onto a continuous 1-min grid.

nodes.name: border_table
nodes.summary: One row per stage border and signal with bend, step, speed, acceleration, jerk and stack bend time.

nodes.name: border_type_curves
nodes.summary: Median signal curves from -45 to +60 min per border type with slopes before/after and bend time.

nodes.name: stage_exits
nodes.summary: Follows every exit from a stage (default Hot standby): slopes after, air level and hours to drop set amounts.

nodes.name: run_all
nodes.summary: Runs the selected analysis parts and writes CSV, JSON and Excel outputs to slopes_jerk/.

nodes.name: twin_fits.py
nodes.summary: Re-derives every fitted constant of the 2D twin (stack heat balance, air-heater efficiency, recuperator, hot-standby cooling law) from project data with scipy optimisers and compares them against the values typed in 05_twin_2d/app.js.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses scipy.optimize minimize (Nelder-Mead) and nnls; a PARTS dict dispatches each fit by name, and app.js constants are scraped with a regex.

nodes.name: frame
nodes.summary: Builds the 1-min frame of plant stages plus air-path columns with replay stretches flagged as held out.

nodes.name: mode10
nodes.summary: Most common value of a series, used for 10-min stage resampling.

nodes.name: fit_heat
nodes.summary: Fits the stack heat balance constants (air exchange, heater heat, loss, gas and current heat) by non-negative least squares.

nodes.name: fit_eaph
nodes.summary: Estimates air-heater efficiency and maximum air-in lift at 6000 ln/min.

nodes.name: fit_targets
nodes.summary: Plant median air-heater setpoints in fuel switch and part load.

nodes.name: tin_sim
nodes.summary: Simulates the app.js air-in temperature model on the plant's stack temperature.

nodes.name: fit_tin
nodes.summary: Grid-searches recuperator effectiveness against measured air-in temperature.

nodes.name: fit_rec
nodes.summary: Fits the lagged recuperator and gas-gain model of the EAPH inlet with Nelder-Mead.

nodes.name: hs_exits
nodes.summary: Extracts hot standby to air-flow cooling exits with per-minute stack and air until the stage ends.

nodes.name: fit_hsc
nodes.summary: Fits the hot-standby cooling law constants on settled exits.

nodes.name: app_values
nodes.summary: Scrapes NAME=value constants typed in 05_twin_2d/app.js.

nodes.name: save
nodes.summary: Merges fitted parts into twin_fits.json and writes a fitted-vs-app.js comparison CSV.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Runs the requested fit parts, saves results and prints the comparison table.

nodes.name: ladder_stages.py
nodes.summary: PLC-style ladder logic that assigns an operating stage to each minute using only present and past signals (timers, seal-in, rung order), reusing operating_states thresholds so both labellings can be compared.
nodes.languageNotes: Emulates PLC on-delay/off-delay timers with pandas shift/cumsum/rolling, and a seal-in scan loop over numpy arrays.

nodes.name: ton
nodes.summary: On-delay timer: true once the input has been true for n consecutive one-minute scans.

nodes.name: tof
nodes.summary: Off-delay timer: keeps the input true for n scans after it drops, bridging short gaps.

nodes.name: contacts
nodes.summary: Builds the boolean input contacts (gas, air, heater, load, rated current, trailing temperature slope) from 1-minute plant signals.

nodes.name: scan
nodes.summary: Runs the ladder rungs top to bottom once per minute with seal-in, returning the closed rung, stage, detail and memory bits.

nodes.name: output_filter
nodes.summary: Debounces the rung output so a new stage is shown only after it holds for n scans; fast rungs pass immediately.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Entry function that turns operating_states 1-minute signals into ladder stage labels by chaining contacts, scan and output_filter.

nodes.name: operating_states.py
nodes.summary: Core segmentation engine that loads one day of downsampled SOFC logger data and labels every minute with an operating stage, gas/air supply phase and operation via row rules, context rules and cross-midnight thermal rules; also writes CSV outputs and timeline plots.
nodes.languageNotes: Rule cascade: per-row classify_row, then block-level passes (merge_short, apply_context, thermal_adjustment) on run-length blocks built with shift/cumsum.

nodes.name: num
nodes.summary: Coerces selected columns to numeric, turning bad values into NaN.

nodes.name: stale
nodes.summary: Returns True when a cached output file is missing or older than any of its source files.

nodes.name: load_signals
nodes.summary: Loads one day's 10 s parquet, derives stack temperature, flows, current, ambient proxy and slopes, and resamples to 1 minute.

nodes.name: steady_hold
nodes.summary: Flags minutes in a steady unloaded 450-550 degC hold with a low temperature slope.

nodes.name: long_hold
nodes.summary: Marks minutes belonging to a steady intermediate hold lasting at least the minimum hold duration.

nodes.name: classify_row
nodes.summary: Per-minute rule cascade that assigns stage and operation from temperature, slope, current and air signals.

nodes.name: gas_phase
nodes.summary: Derives the gas/air supply phase of each minute from the flow controllers (forming gas, natural gas, air only, off).

nodes.name: fuel_rules
nodes.summary: Applies the natural-gas rules (user decision 2026-10-15) to stage blocks.

nodes.name: ng_tail
nodes.summary: Returns the trailing natural-gas minutes of a block.

nodes.name: plant_off_cold
nodes.summary: True when the plant is fully off: Idle stage or shut down at ambient.

nodes.name: blocks
nodes.summary: Assigns a run-length block id to each contiguous stage/operation stretch.

nodes.name: merge_short
nodes.summary: Absorbs blocks shorter than the minimum segment length into the preceding block.

nodes.name: apply_context
nodes.summary: Large block-level pass applying context rules a single row cannot see (neighbouring stages, previous-day stage, restarts, cold plant).

nodes.name: restarts_next_day
nodes.summary: Checks whether the next day file starts with a warm, off plant that then restarts without load.

nodes.name: thermal_adjustment
nodes.summary: Final stage rules (user decisions 2026-10-14 and later) reclassifying warm cooling, restarts and natural-gas tails.

nodes.name: sub_stage
nodes.summary: Returns the Shut-down sub-stage name: Cooling or At ambient.

nodes.name: prev_day
nodes.summary: Finds the latest earlier day file within the allowed gap, or None.

nodes.name: last_stage
nodes.summary: Returns the stage at the end of a day file, used by rules that cross midnight.

nodes.name: segment
nodes.summary: Main pipeline for one day: loads signals, classifies rows, applies phase, fuel, context and thermal rules, and returns minute states plus a segment table.

nodes.name: count_episodes
nodes.summary: Counts how many separate times each stage occurs in one day's minute table.

nodes.name: stage_minutes
nodes.summary: Counts minutes per stage including No data.

nodes.name: segment_all
nodes.summary: Segments every available day and returns states and segments per day.

nodes.name: plot_flows
nodes.summary: Plots anode-side flows (N2, NG, H2) and cathode air on given axes.

nodes.name: phase_band
nodes.summary: Draws one coloured span per contiguous gas/air supply phase.

nodes.name: plot
nodes.summary: Builds the daily timeline figure of stack temperature, current, flows, phases and stages; saves or returns it.

nodes.name: stage_signals.py
nodes.summary: Shared loader for the per-stage analysis notebooks that joins episode-library stage labels with extra flow, BOP temperature, voltage and setpoint signals on a 1-minute grid, plus helpers for episode neighbours and heat-up/cool-down band rates.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Loads library labels and joins extra 1-minute signals from all days, blanks logger dropouts and derives air-flow and fuel-utilisation columns.

nodes.name: episodes
nodes.summary: Reads the episode library table of stage episodes.

nodes.name: all_cuts
nodes.summary: Reads every logged cut event from the trip cut CSV, unfiltered.

nodes.name: neighbours
nodes.summary: Adds previous/next stage and gaps in minutes to each library episode.

nodes.name: band_rates
nodes.summary: Computes degC/h heating or cooling rates across temperature bands from first or last crossings.

nodes.name: robust_sigma
nodes.summary: Estimates the noise sigma of a 1-minute series from the MAD of its first differences.

nodes.name: stage_split.py
nodes.summary: Splits the 1 Hz raw parquet logger data into one parquet file per stage episode (Shut-down split into Cooling and At-ambient sub-stages), writing index and summary CSVs, and provides loaders for a stage or an episode.

nodes.name: stage_dir
nodes.summary: Returns the output folder for a stage and optional Shut-down sub-stage.

nodes.name: file_id
nodes.summary: Builds the output file id from episode id and sub-stage suffix.

nodes.name: file_path
nodes.summary: Returns the parquet path for an episode file.

nodes.name: load_labels
nodes.summary: Loads per-minute stage labels and assigns output file ids.

nodes.name: pieces
nodes.summary: Builds one row per output file with start/end and episode metadata.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Writes every stage episode file from 1 Hz day parquets, plus index.csv and summary.csv.

nodes.name: summary
nodes.summary: Summarises files, hours and rows per stage and sub-stage.

nodes.name: load_stage
nodes.summary: Loads all 1 s rows of one stage (optionally a sub-stage, columns, training-only) as one DataFrame.

nodes.name: load_episode
nodes.summary: Loads one episode's 1 s data, joining both Shut-down sub-stages.

nodes.name: flow_check.py
nodes.summary: Stitches all daily operating-stage segmentations into one timeline and checks every stage episode (transitions, heat-up/cool-down rates, hold temperatures, load ramps, stack temperature limit) against operational-modes.md, writing episodes, checks and per-day verdict CSVs.
nodes.languageNotes: Dispatches per-stage check functions through a dict (CHECKS) mapping stage name to callable; each returns (name, value, lo, hi, limit) tuples judged against a tolerance-widened range.

nodes.name: industrial_stages.py
nodes.summary: Maps the project's operating stages onto industry stage codes S0-S8 (IEC 62282-3-200 / PackML style), carving out protective-trip windows from trip_check cut events as the new stage S8 and writing industrial episode and trip-window tables.

nodes.name: trip_check.py
nodes.summary: Checks S-PLC trip conditions against the 1 s raw parquet logger data and detects emergency shutdowns (purge / stop / power cuts) by recognising the abrupt cuts of current, heater power and gas the safety PLC performs.

nodes.name: stitch
nodes.summary: Segments each requested day with operating_states.segment (stdout suppressed) and concatenates them into one sorted timeline so midnight-crossing stages form one episode.

nodes.name: episodes
nodes.summary: Splits the stitched timeline into stage episodes (also breaking on logger gaps), recording operation sequence, phases, sub-stages, days covered and the previous episode.

nodes.name: band_rate
nodes.summary: Computes the average temperature rate (degC/h) while a series passes between a top and bottom temperature band.

nodes.name: check_startup
nodes.summary: Checks a Start-up episode: heat-up rate vs documented range and the 120 degC/h limit, the ~510 degC hold length against the 6 h rule, and the forming-gas switch temperature.

nodes.name: check_standby
nodes.summary: Checks a Hot standby episode for constant temperature, its hold level (about 510 degC low hold or 575-610 degC) and the 6 h low-hold rule.

nodes.name: check_load
nodes.summary: Checks Part load / Rated power episodes for per-string current ramp rate against the documented 0.3-0.9 A/min band and the 1 A/min limit.

nodes.name: check_shutdown
nodes.summary: Checks a Shut-down episode's cooling rates in the 600-300 degC and 300-100 degC bands, natural cooling, and that it ends within 30 K of ambient.

nodes.name: check_adjust
nodes.summary: Checks a Thermal adjustment episode (no-load re-heat or cool-back of a hot stack) for temperature range and rate.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Runs the full flow check: stitches days, builds episodes, applies transition, temperature-limit and stage-specific checks, and aggregates per-day verdicts.

nodes.name: trip_events
nodes.summary: Loads (or recomputes and caches) trip_check cut events and keeps only protective trip kinds of a hot stack (at or above 400 degC).

nodes.name: trip_windows
nodes.summary: Chains trip cuts within 30 min into single trips and builds S8 time windows ending 15 min after the last cut.

nodes.name: add_codes
nodes.summary: Adds the industry code (S0-S8) and label columns to a segmented day, overriding rows inside trip windows with S8.

nodes.name: blocks
nodes.summary: Collapses consecutive rows with the same code into blocks with start/end, stack temperatures, max current and mean EAPH power.

nodes.name: runs
nodes.summary: Returns run ids for a label series, starting a new run on label change or a logger gap longer than EPISODE_GAP_H; shared with flow_check.

nodes.name: episodes
nodes.summary: Builds the industrial-episode table across all days and assigns cold/warm/hot start classes to Start-up episodes.

nodes.name: run_all
nodes.summary: Segments every day via operating_states.segment_all, finds trip windows and adds S0-S8 codes and blocks per day.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Reads selected columns of one day's 1 s raw parquet file, de-duplicating timestamps and coercing to numeric.

nodes.name: trip_margins
nodes.summary: Per day, reports max/min of each S-PLC trip sensor (temperatures, pressure, insulation) against its trip value.

nodes.name: _classify
nodes.summary: Classifies an abrupt cut as emergency purge, emergency stop, or power cut from valve, current, heater and air signals before and after.

nodes.name: cut_events
nodes.summary: Scans all days for abrupt cuts of current, heater power or gas, classifies them and records context such as stack temperature and sensors near trip values.

nodes.name: exhaust_crossings
nodes.summary: Finds exhaust temperature crossings of the day's trip value and links each to the nearest following cut event.

nodes.name: plot_event
nodes.summary: Plots a three-panel matplotlib view of temperatures, current/air and valve states around one event time.

nodes.name: pattern_app.py
nodes.summary: Streamlit GUI over the synthetic-data generator: the user picks total hours and per-stage counts, sees the random stage pattern as a timeline, stage-map chart and gas/air supply-phase table, then fills it with real 1-min sensor data via pattern_filler.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Streamlit cache wrappers so the real-episode library and flow medians load once per session; charts are built with Altair.

nodes.name: pattern_filler.py
nodes.summary: Fills a stage pattern block by block with real sensor minutes: picks matching real episodes from library/episodes.csv, fits their length (window, time-warp or chained cool-downs) and blends temperatures/pressures at the joins to produce a full synthetic 1-min dataset.

nodes.name: pattern_generator.py
nodes.summary: Generates a random SOFC stage pattern for a given total time and stage counts, following the allowed stage-map arrows and real duration ranges, and plans each block's gas/air supply phases with gas permissive rules G1-G10 enforced by fix_gas.

nodes.name: sofc_theme
nodes.summary: Registers the app's Altair chart theme (Inter font, muted inks, light grid, large axis labels).

nodes.name: stage_map
nodes.summary: Builds the Altair stage-map chart of every allowed stage transition, highlighting the arrows the current pattern uses.

nodes.name: real_minutes
nodes.summary: Loads (and caches) the preprocessed 1-min real sensor data with stage, sub-stage, episode and gas-phase labels, optionally rebuilding the cache.

nodes.name: raw_extra
nodes.summary: Reads extra raw sensor tags (e.g. FIRC 1,1,3) missing from the preprocessed files and resamples them to 1-min means.

nodes.name: Library
nodes.summary: Holds the real episode table with previous/next stages and lazily builds gap-free 1-min sensor frames per episode, plus supply-phase mix and dry-forming-gas lookups.

nodes.name: day_folder
nodes.summary: Resolves the output folder for a filled synthetic day next to its pattern plan.

nodes.name: hold
nodes.summary: Fills a Hot standby or Idle block with a scored random window of one real episode, mirroring short episodes forward-backward and keeping planned natural-gas tail minutes at the end.

nodes.name: path
nodes.summary: Fills a Start-up, Thermal adjustment or Part load block by picking a scored real episode and time-warping it to the block length.

nodes.name: chain
nodes.summary: Fills a Shut-down block with a chain of real cool-down pieces, each entered at the minute it passes the current stack temperature so real cooling rates are kept.

nodes.name: fill
nodes.summary: Main filling routine: walks each pattern block, dispatches to hold/path/chain, blends joins, labels plant stages and returns the synthetic sensor frame plus a per-block report.

nodes.name: plot
nodes.summary: Saves a PNG overview of the filled synthetic data with stack temperature and stage bands.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry: reads or generates a pattern, fills it with real data and writes the CSV (and optional plot) to the day folder.

nodes.name: day_dir
nodes.summary: Returns the default datasets/seed_<seed> output folder for a pattern.

nodes.name: with_air
nodes.summary: Splits the forming-gas phase into with/without cathode air by checking the cathode air flow controllers.

nodes.name: split_arrows
nodes.summary: Rewrites the allowed stage-map arrows so Shut-down is split into Cooling and At ambient sub-stages, entered only from Hot standby.

nodes.name: step_name
nodes.summary: Combines a stage and optional Shut-down sub-stage into a single step label.

nodes.name: parse_pairs
nodes.summary: Parses 'Stage=value, ...' text into a dict keyed by canonical stage names.

nodes.name: library_bounds
nodes.summary: Derives min-max duration bounds per step from the real episode library.

nodes.name: library_counts
nodes.summary: Counts real episodes per step in the library to use as default stage counts.

nodes.name: to_ambient_min_h
nodes.summary: Estimates the minimum hours a Cooling block needs to bring the stack from operating temperature to ambient +30 K, from the fastest real cool-down.

nodes.name: order
nodes.summary: Randomly orders the requested stage counts into a sequence that only uses allowed arrows, inserting filler stages when needed.

nodes.name: durations
nodes.summary: Draws random block lengths within each step's bounds that add up exactly to the total hours.

nodes.name: runs_of
nodes.summary: Compresses a per-minute phase series into (phase, minutes) runs.

nodes.name: phase_profiles
nodes.summary: Collects real supply-phase run profiles per step, keyed by the following step, from the labelled data.

nodes.name: scale_runs
nodes.summary: Stretches a real phase-run profile to a block length while keeping natural-gas runs outside Part load at their real minutes.

nodes.name: parse_phases
nodes.summary: Parses a phases text column back into (phase, minutes) runs.

nodes.name: phases_text
nodes.summary: Serializes phase runs into a compact text form for the pattern CSV.

nodes.name: gas_faults
nodes.summary: Checks a block's supply-phase plan against the gas permissive rules G1-G10 and returns the rule ids it violates.

nodes.name: fix_gas
nodes.summary: Minimally edits a block's supply-phase plan so it satisfies the gas permissive rules, reporting what was fixed.

nodes.name: plan_phases
nodes.summary: Assigns each pattern step a gas/air supply plan copied from a real stretch of the same step, scaled and gas-fixed, with a gas_check result.

nodes.name: flow_medians
nodes.summary: Computes median flow-controller values per supply phase from the real data.

nodes.name: flow_levels
nodes.summary: Returns per-phase flow levels (ln/min) used by the GUI and phase table.

nodes.name: phase_table
nodes.summary: Expands a pattern into a per-phase table with start/end times and median flows.

nodes.name: plot
nodes.summary: Saves a timeline PNG of the stage pattern and its supply phases.

nodes.name: generate
nodes.summary: Core generator: canonicalises counts, orders stages, draws durations and plans supply phases, returning the pattern DataFrame.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry that parses arguments, generates a pattern, writes the CSV and optional plot.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Index of the plant reference folder listing the flow diagram, sensor layout, stage definitions, component sensor map, literature notes and sensor spreadsheets, and which analysis scripts read them.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Landing-page design skill guide (strategy, layout, copywriting, SEO, typography, spacing, motion, ship checklist); generic web-design reference unrelated to the SOFC analysis itself.

nodes.name: component_sensor_map_en.md
nodes.summary: Instrument map of the SOFC plant by component (cathode air, POx/N2/H2, natural gas, air preheaters, reformer, afterburner, stack manifolds, per-string electrical tags) plus the S-PLC safety-trip limits for emergency purge and emergency stop.

nodes.name: operational-modes-current.md
nodes.summary: Current definition of the eight plant stages with thresholds, stage order and mapping to the older stages and edge modes, as implemented in plant_stages.py and the operating-states notebook.

nodes.name: operational-modes.md
nodes.summary: Original operating-state definitions for the SOFC plant: state transitions, measured flows per state, data-derived heat-up/cool-down and load ramp rates against Elcogen limits, and edge-attribute mode identifiers; cited by section number in analysis scripts.

nodes.name: sofc-operational-stage-literature.md
nodes.summary: Literature notes comparing SOFC operational-stage terminology across the LG patent family, data-center papers and Bloom Energy, with a source matrix and open gaps.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: User and developer guide for the SOFC Plant Descriptive Twin v3.x: version history, how to open/install the app, saving and replaying datasets, the file layout, rebuilding data with tools/prep.py and tools/bends.py, and how sensor readings, warming slopes and stage changes are computed in app.js.

nodes.name: app.bat
nodes.summary: Windows launcher that opens index.html as a chromeless Edge (or Chrome fallback) app window via a properly encoded file:/// URI, no server needed.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a PowerShell [uri] cast inside a for /f loop to percent-encode the path so folders with # or % still load.

nodes.name: index.html
nodes.summary: Single-page markup for the SOFC Plant Descriptive Twin v3.5: top bar, stage bar, clickable plant schematic and trend panels; loads Google Fonts, style.css, the PWA manifest, generated data/sensors.js and data/bends.js, then app.js, and registers the service worker when served over HTTP.
nodes.languageNotes: A tiny inline script reads the saved theme from localStorage before CSS loads to avoid a light/dark flash.

nodes.name: install_shortcut.bat

nodes.name: cold_idle_analysis.ipynb
nodes.summary: Analyses plant-off hours (Idle and Shut-down at rest) over all 39 days: episode inventory, stack settling temperature versus ambient, passive cooling physics, timings and the signal order when a start-up leaves the off state; ends with synthetic-generator inputs and open points.
nodes.languageNotes: Jupyter notebook that puts 03_data_analysis/scripts on sys.path and imports shared helper modules from there.

nodes.name: excel_sensor_analysis.ipynb

nodes.name: heater_temperatures.ipynb
nodes.summary: Compares stack temperature with the gas-line heater thermocouples (ERH, EAGH, EAOH1-3) per consecutive-day stretch and per decided plant stage, including heater-minus-stack offsets, distributions and safety thermocouples against trip limits.
nodes.languageNotes: Jupyter notebook that puts 03_data_analysis/scripts on sys.path and imports shared helper modules from there.

nodes.name: industrial_stages.ipynb
nodes.summary: Maps the operating stages of all day files to industry stage codes S0-S8: segmentation, timelines, a trip in detail, hours and episodes per stage, transition counts, start classes and every S8 trip with surrounding stages.
nodes.languageNotes: Jupyter notebook that puts 03_data_analysis/scripts on sys.path and imports shared helper modules from there.

nodes.name: operating_states.ipynb
nodes.summary: Central stage-labelling notebook: derives operating stages from the operational-modes rules, checks limits, counts stages per day over 39 day files, analyses trip conditions on 1 s data, and in section 12 builds the 8 decided plant stages with per-stage sensor plots.
nodes.languageNotes: Jupyter notebook that puts 03_data_analysis/scripts on sys.path and imports shared helper modules from there.

nodes.name: part_load_analysis.ipynb
nodes.summary: Studies part-load runs: current ramp rates against the 1 A/min limit, string voltage versus current and balance, stack and exhaust heating with the 200 C trip, fuel/air/heater levels, how runs end, distance to rated power and signals per current band.
nodes.languageNotes: Jupyter notebook that puts 03_data_analysis/scripts on sys.path and imports shared helper modules from there.

nodes.name: preprocessing.ipynb
nodes.summary: Cleans the raw SOFC logger files: column inventory and missing values, per-day column statistics, column classification and selection of stage-detection sensors, export of the cleaned dataset, column groups for plotting and plots of continuous day runs.
nodes.languageNotes: Jupyter notebook that puts 03_data_analysis/scripts on sys.path and imports shared helper modules from there.

nodes.name: rated_power_extrapolation.ipynb
nodes.summary: Stretches every part-load sensor to rated power (30 A, 52 kW) and 60 kW: straight-line fits per sensor, leave-one-run-out trust checks, electrical V-I-gas solution, R2 of every fit, curve and time-lag model comparison and best-curve extrapolation with saved outputs.
nodes.languageNotes: Jupyter notebook that puts 03_data_analysis/scripts on sys.path and imports shared helper modules from there.

nodes.name: sensors_by_stage.ipynb
nodes.summary: Splits 156 sensors by operating stage, describes each sensor inside each stage, tests whether 106 non-stage sensors can be predicted from the 50 stage-rule sensors with regression models, and assigns a class and synthetic-data recipe per stage-sensor pair.

nodes.name: shutdown_analysis.ipynb
nodes.summary: Analyses shut-down episodes over all 39 days: cool-down band rates, forced-cooling rate against the 120 C/h limit and its physics, air/gas/heater sequence on the way down, thermal gradients, timings and signal levels by temperature band.
nodes.languageNotes: Jupyter notebook that puts 03_data_analysis/scripts on sys.path and imports shared helper modules from there.

nodes.name: column_groups.json
nodes.summary: Groups all retained logger columns by instrument family (TIR, TIRC, TIRZ, PIR, FIRC, EIRC voltage/current/power) for plotting in the preprocessing notebook.

nodes.name: column_groups.json
nodes.summary: Smaller column grouping for the stage-detection sensor subset: ambient and stack thermocouples, cathode inlet temperature, inlet air pressure and string electrical signals.

nodes.name: availability.py
nodes.summary: Computes SOFC plant availability metrics (AF, SF, FOR, inherent and equivalent availability, MTBF) from the decided plant stages and trip windows, under strict and lenient post-trip rules, writing summary and trip-recovery CSVs.

nodes.name: trip_recovery
nodes.summary: Per trip, finds when the plant was ready again and whether it was cooled down in between.

nodes.name: numbers
nodes.summary: Classifies minutes into power/ready/planned/forced buckets for a selection and computes the IEEE-762-style availability figures.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Loads stages and trips, builds trip recovery, and writes availability summaries for the whole period and per month under both post-trip rules.

nodes.name: correlation_common.py
nodes.summary: CLI that computes Pearson and Spearman correlation across all columns of the common dataset (one day or all days), drops constant/sparse columns and writes matrices, ranked pairs, an Excel workbook and clustered heatmaps.

nodes.name: load_day
nodes.summary: Reads one tab-separated decimal-comma day file with pyarrow and resamples it to mean values.

nodes.name: top_pairs
nodes.summary: Ranks all column pairs by absolute Pearson and Spearman correlation.

nodes.name: heatmap
nodes.summary: Draws a clustered correlation heatmap in a given column order and saves it as PNG.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Parses CLI options, loads days in parallel, filters columns by coverage, computes both correlation matrices and writes all outputs.

nodes.name: downsample.py
nodes.summary: Builds missing 1 s parquet and 10 s downsampled parquet files from raw logger text files, reproducing the original files exactly, with a check mode comparing rebuilt output to disk.

nodes.name: raw_to_parquet
nodes.summary: Parses a raw tab-separated decimal-comma logger file into a 1 s parquet with the original dtypes and header handling.

nodes.name: downsample
nodes.summary: Averages a 1 s day file into clock-aligned 10 s windows, building the 1 s parquet first when it is missing.

nodes.name: check
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a day in memory and reports any shape, column or value difference against the stored 10 s file.

nodes.name: efficiency_check.py
nodes.summary: Script estimating gross electrical efficiency, fuel utilisation (compared with PLC rFU_Worst tags), after-heater efficiency and per-string efficiency from the parquet data, since no efficiency tag is logged.

nodes.name: rated_power_curves.py
nodes.summary: Fits line, quadratic and first-order-lag model families to every part-load sensor, picks the best by leave-one-run-out MAE, writes the best plausible steady-state value into the rated-power table and plots all fits to PDF.

nodes.name: fit_sensor
nodes.summary: Fits all model families for one sensor and returns coefficients, predictions, R2, MAE and leave-one-run-out MAE.

nodes.name: at_power
nodes.summary: Evaluates a fitted model at steady power p, treating the lag term as equal to power.

nodes.name: fit_all
nodes.summary: Builds lagged power series for all time constants, fits every sensor, and returns the best-model table plus per-sensor fits.

nodes.name: apply_best
nodes.summary:
Writes each sensor's best plausible curve into the use_

kW columns of the extrapolation table and records the model name.

nodes.name: plot_rows
nodes.summary: Plots reading versus power and reading over the part-load minutes for a set of sensors.

nodes.name: plot_all
nodes.summary: Writes every fitted sensor to a multi-page A4 PDF, six rows per page.

nodes.name: self_check
nodes.summary: Assert-based self-test of the lag and model fitting on synthetic runs.

nodes.name: rated_power_extrapolation.py
nodes.summary: Extrapolates every logged sensor from part load to rated power (30 A, 52 kW) and 60 kW with straight lines in DC power, solves string V-I and natural-gas flow consistently, and adds trip and limit notes to the output table.

nodes.name: pl_minutes
nodes.summary: Selects part-load minutes from the plant-stage file, joins the downsampled sensor data and numbers each run.

nodes.name: extrapolate
nodes.summary: Fits a robust straight line per changing sensor against DC power, scores it by leave-one-run-out error and reads it at every power step.

nodes.name: add_notes
nodes.summary: Annotates extrapolated sensors that cross trip limits, cell protection or actuator 0/100 % bounds.

nodes.name: electrical
nodes.summary: Solves per-string V=a+bI lines at equal string current so sum V*I matches each power step, and adds Faraday natural-gas flow.

nodes.name: stage_crosswalk.py
nodes.summary: Translates each minute into a plant-neutral sensor signature (thermal, trend, supply, load, trip, been-hot) and maps it onto several stage vocabularies (own S0-S8, LG patent, Hanasaki, Bloom) with match grades.

nodes.summary: Derives the plant-neutral facts of each minute from stack temperature, slope, current, gas phase and trip flag.

nodes.summary: Reads the industrial-stage minutes, builds signatures, translates into every vocabulary and writes the crosswalk outputs.

nodes.summary: Traces every tag in the Excel visualization-tool sensor list to a logged data column and computes usefulness metrics per tag, writing trace CSVs.

nodes.name: classify.py
nodes.summary: Assigns a verdict per Excel sensor tag (traceability and usefulness) from the trace metrics, using plant area, sensors already used in code, control/safety twins and parallel line pairs.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the root README, the project's start page: it maps the folders, gives entry points by goal, and draws the data flow from raw logger data through the stage scripts to synthetic data and the 2D twin. It also introduces the 8 plant stages that every later step relies on. requirements.txt lists the Python 3.13 libraries (pandas, pyarrow, scipy, scikit-learn, streamlit, jupyterlab, pytest) and notes which part of the project needs each one.

tour.title: The Plant Reference
tour.description: Before reading any code, learn the plant itself. operational-modes.md holds the original operating-state definitions with transitions, flows and heat-up/cool-down limits, and operational-modes-current.md defines the eight decided plant stages and their thresholds as later implemented in code. component_sensor_map_en.md lists the instruments by plant component together with the safety-PLC trip limits, so you can decode tags like TIR, FIRC and EIRC when they appear later.

tour.title: Cleaning the Logger Data
tour.description: Everything starts with 39 days of raw logger files. downsample.py rebuilds 1 s and 10 s parquet files from the raw text logs, and preprocessing.ipynb inventories columns, handles missing values and picks the sensors used for stage detection. The stage column_groups.json records that smaller sensor subset (stack thermocouples, cathode inlet, air pressure, string electrical signals) that the stage rules in the next step read.
tour.languageLesson: Parquet is a columnar file format: reading a few sensor columns out of hundreds is fast because each column is stored separately, which is why the project converts text logs to parquet once and then works from those files.

tour.title: Core Segmentation Engine
tour.description: operating_states.py is the most depended-upon file in the project (22 incoming links). It loads one day of downsampled data and labels every minute with an operating stage, a gas/air supply phase and an operation, using row rules, context rules and a cross-midnight thermal rule built on the definitions from Step 2. operating_states.ipynb is the central notebook that derives and checks these labels over all 39 days and, in section 12, builds the eight decided plant stages.

tour.title: Trips and Industry Stages
tour.description: Safety trips need special handling because they happen within seconds. trip_check.py works on the 1 s data to spot emergency shutdowns by the abrupt cuts of current, heater power and gas made by the safety PLC. industrial_stages.py then maps the stages from Step 4 onto industry codes S0-S8 (IEC 62282-3-200 / PackML style) and turns the trip windows into their own stage, S8.

tour.title: The Eight Plant Stages
tour.description: plant_stages.py, the second most depended-upon module, combines operating_states.py with the trip windows from industrial_stages.py to define the eight decided plant stages (Heat-up air through Trip: purge). It labels every logged minute and writes the 1-minute stage parquet that most later analyses read. test_rules.py protects this logic with small fake timelines that have known answers for stage buckets, gas-based rules and trip chaining.
tour.languageLesson: pytest finds functions named test_* and runs them. Building tiny synthetic timelines with known answers is a good way to test rule-based classifiers: each test pins down one rule without needing the real 39-day dataset.

tour.title: Question-Driven Notebooks
tour.description: With stages in place, the analysis is organised as one notebook per question; the data-analysis README lists them in reading order with each one's output folder. stage_signals.py is the shared loader that joins stage labels with extra flow, temperature and setpoint signals on a 1-minute grid. The start-up, shut-down and part-load notebooks then measure rates against plant limits, sequences and signal levels, and these numbers later feed the synthetic generator.

tour.title: Slopes and Twin Physics
tour.description: Two scripts turn stage-labelled data into numbers the twin can use. slopes_jerk.py measures how fast temperatures rise and fall in each stage and how sharply curves bend at stage borders, and border_type_curves.json saves the typical curve for each border type. twin_fits.py uses scipy optimisers to re-derive the twin's fitted constants (stack heat balance, air-heater efficiency, recuperator, hot-standby cooling), saving them in twin_fits.json for comparison with the values typed into the twin app.

tour.title: Plant Performance Metrics
tour.description: These scripts answer the business questions on top of the stages. availability.py computes availability factor, forced outage rate and MTBF from the plant stages and trip windows, under strict and lenient post-trip rules. efficiency_check.py estimates efficiency and fuel use because no efficiency tag is logged, and rated_power_extrapolation.py stretches every part-load sensor to rated power (30 A, 52 kW) and 60 kW.

tour.title: Synthetic Data Pipeline
tour.description: The synthetic-data folder reuses the real episodes to make new plant data, in the steps its README describes. build_library.py cuts the approved stage segmentation into an episode library, pattern_generator.py makes a random stage sequence that follows the allowed stage transitions and real durations, and pattern_filler.py fills each block with matching real sensor minutes, blending values at the joins. pattern_app.py puts a Streamlit interface on top so a user can choose hours and stage counts and see the result.
tour.languageLesson: Streamlit reruns the whole Python script top to bottom on every widget change. That makes simple GUIs quick to write, but slow steps should be cached so they do not repeat on each click.

tour.title: Building Twin Data
tour.description: The twin is a static browser app, so the analysis results are baked into JavaScript data files at build time. tools/prep.py fits about 111 plant sensors per stage against stack temperature and writes data/sensors.js, while tools/bends.py uses slopes_jerk.py from Step 8 to write the stage-border curves in data/bends.js. Both generated files set a window global, which the twin loads without needing a server.

tour.title: The 2D Digital Twin
tour.description: app.js is the core of the SOFC Plant Descriptive Twin: a fitted stack heat-balance model with stage rules, buttons for start, load, rated power, shutdown and trip, sensor readings that ease between stages, and a clickable SVG plant diagram with trend plots. index.html lays out the stage bar, schematic and trend panels and loads the generated data from Step 11, and style.css holds the dark/light theme plus fixed colours for each plant fluid. The twin README covers version history, usage and how to rebuild the data.

tour.title: Running the Twin Offline
tour.description: The twin ships as an installable local app with no back end. app.bat opens index.html in a chromeless Edge window straight from disk, and start.bat serves the folder on port 8765 so the service worker and PWA install work. sw.js keeps an offline copy using network-first fetching with a cache fallback, and manifest.webmanifest gives the app its name, theme and icons.
tour.languageLesson: A service worker is a script the browser runs apart from the page that can intercept network requests. 'Network-first with cache fallback' always tries fresh files and serves the stored copy only when offline. Service workers only run over http(s), not file://, which is why start.bat starts a local server.

tour.title: Twin-Driven Datasets
tour.description: The final piece closes the loop: twin_dataset.js runs the unchanged app.js from Step 12 in a Node vm sandbox and presses its buttons to produce months of minute data with a chosen availability and stage counts. The dataset app (dataset_app.bat, a localhost-only server.js and its index.html) wraps this in a form with progress and saved-dataset browsing. make_tables.py turns a run into relational CSV tables (readings, stages, components, sensors) for downstream use.
tour.languageLesson: Node's vm module runs code in a separate global context. By giving it stub DOM objects, browser code such as app.js can run headless on the command line, so the simulator and the twin never drift apart.
